latin: MUNDA cor meum, ac lábia mea, omnípotens Deus, qui lábia Isaíæ Prophétæ cálculo mundásti igníto : ita me tua grata miseratióne dignáre mundáre, ut sanctum Evangélium tuum digne váleam nuntiáre. Per Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
notes: Whole black prayer body at the lower right of printed p. 274, following the rubric for the deacon at solemn Mass; printed p. 275 explicitly reuses Munda cor meum ut supra for the priest celebrating without deacon and subdeacon. The following Jube, domne, benedicere request is separate and excluded. The drop initial and following small capitals are joined as MUNDA. No cross or dialogue head mark is printed inside this body.

latin: Per evangélica dicta deleántur nostra delícta.
notes: Whole black prayer sentence inside the left-column rubric describing the priest kissing the Gospel after its solemn proclamation. The right-column rubric for Mass without sacred ministers refers back to it ut supra. No Amen, cross or dialogue head mark is printed in this sentence; surrounding red rubrics and the minister response are excluded.

latin: Dóminus sit in corde meo, et in lábiis meis : ut digne et competénter annúntiem Evangélium suum. Amen.
notes: Whole black first-person prayer at the lower left of printed p. 275, under the rubric for the priest celebrating without deacon and subdeacon. The separate Jube, Domine, benedicere request above it and the upper-left second-person Dominus sit in corde tuo blessing of the deacon are excluded. No cross or dialogue head mark is printed inside this body.
